title: Canonical state hashing silently drops a data key named __proto__, producing hash collisions between differing world states
source: Independent external review by GPT-6 Astra via Kaggle Benchmarks task review-ce-stack v2, claim independently re-verified against source by an explorer agent
evidence: src/core/hash.ts:9-10: const out: Record<string, unknown> = {}; for (const k of Object.keys(obj).sort()) out[k] = sortKeys(obj[k]);
Assignment out["__proto__"] = v does not create an own data property: with an object value it reassigns the prototype, with a primitive it is silently ignored
JSON.stringify serialises only own enumerable properties, so the key vanishes from the hashed payload
src/core/persistence.ts:458 restores worlds via raw JSON.parse(text), which DOES create own "__proto__" data properties - so the key is reachable through the documented restore path
src/core/types.ts:169: Entity.attrs is Record<string, number | string | boolean>, i.e. arbitrary string keys are permitted
grep across src/ returns zero occurrences of __proto__, Object.create(null, or defineProperty - no guard and no regression test exists
impact: A world whose entity attributes contain a own key "__proto__" hashes identically to a world without it. stateHash is the package's core content-addressed determinism guarantee (state identity, checkpoint equality, replay, cross-host verification), so two materially different states can compare equal. Reachable only if such a key is ever introduced; no current test or fixture does so, so no existing result is invalidated.
root_cause: Canonicalisation rebuilds objects using plain property assignment instead of defining own data properties (or null-prototype objects). The canonical input domain was never specified or validated, so prototype-sensitive keys were never considered.
why_2: The canonical form was implemented with ordinary object literals rather than Object.create(null) or Object.defineProperty.
why_3: No written canonical-input model exists that enumerates supported key and value domains.
why_4: The hashing boundary was treated as an internal detail rather than a contract with adversarial-input obligations.
detection_gap: All determinism and persistence tests use reference fixtures that never contain a prototype-polluting key, so identical hashes across runs cannot reveal the omission.
corrective_action_required: Preserve __proto__ as an ordinary data key in sortKeys (defineProperty or null-prototype objects)
Define and document the supported canonical input model; explicitly reject unsupported values rather than silently dropping them
Add regression tests for key preservation, key ordering and rejection behaviour
Add a differential hash test where two worlds differ only by a __proto__ key and must produce different hashes
Confirm whether any published checkpoint in the wild could be affected
verdict_of_verification: TRUE - defect confirmed by independent code inspection

resolution.fix: src/core/hash.ts sortKeys now special-cases k === '__proto__' with Object.defineProperty(out, k, {value: sortKeys(obj[k]), enumerable: true, writable: true, configurable: true}); all other keys keep the original fast-path assignment
resolution.regression_test: src/poc/hash-proto.test.ts (6 cases: own-key survival, stateHash collision broken, JSON.parse persistence round-trip, golden zero-drift literals, nested/array recursion, primitive value no-crash)
resolution.verification: VER-2026-002-hash-fix-kaggle (PASS) - independent Kaggle CPU run at commit 552c218: defect live pre-fix (collides=true), eliminated post-fix (collides=false), zero hash drift across 3 seeds, 752/752 tests pass, 19.83M-tick soak
resolution.scope_note: Fix is limited to the __proto__ special case to preserve zero hash drift (P-019). The NCR's broader corrective actions (documented canonical input model, explicit rejection of unsupported values) remain open as follow-up work and are reflected in the Astra v3 top fixes.
resolution.residual_risk: The canonical input domain is still undocumented; other prototype-sensitive keys were not in scope. Astra v3 still rates the closed-validation-loop risk as the biggest hidden risk.
